Purpose
With
--moe-backend humming
and expert parallelism, Humming runs DeepSeek-V4.1's MXFP4 experts on its grouped GEMM. On Hopper the indexed GEMM is much faster for this model. This PR makes
get_humming_moe_gemm_type()
return
indexed
when all of these hold:
the experts are MXFP4 with DeepSeek V4 routing;
model_type
is
deepseek_v41
or
deepseek_v41_text
;
the device is CUDA SM90;
there are no all2all kernels, or the backend is
allgather_reducescatter
.
Without EP, Humming already picks indexed, so nothing changes there.
VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE
still overrides the choice. Since
#56997
, Humming is the default MXFP4 MoE backend on SM90, so V4.1 with EP on Hopper otherwise runs the grouped GEMM by default; this PR moves that default path to indexed too. The rule applies with BF16 activations and with per-token FP8 activations (
--quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
).
The MXFP4 MoE method (DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3, plain mxfp4) now runs
quantization_config.moe.activation
:
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --moe-backend humming --quantization-config.moe.activation fp8_per_token
Humming takes the named format as a fixed input schema, with its input-schema fallback off.
Other explicit backends must run the named format, and
auto
keeps only the backends that do. Before, these models ignored the name on every backend. Now a backend that does not run it stops vLLM, on every platform (CUDA, ROCm, XPU, CPU). The DeepSeek V4 MegaMoE backends (
deep_gemm_mega_moe
,
aiter_mega_moe
) build their own experts and do not read the name. On ROCm, the Kimi-K3 AITER path, which skips the backend selector, now refuses a named activation instead of ignoring it. For example,
fp8_per_token
with
flashinfer_trtllm
now stops vLLM instead of running MXFP8. A draft model with its own
speculative_config.moe_backend
inherits the target's
quantization_config
, so the same rule applies to it.
The startup log prints the format Humming runs:
Humming MoE activations: fp8_per_token (group size 0, scale dtype float32)
. The line appears for every Humming MoE model, gpt-oss included.
On SM90 Humming,
mxfp8
and
fp8_per_block_dynamic
stop vLLM at startup, before the weights load. Humming has no e8m0 input scales on WGMMA, and humming 0.1.16 rejects fp32 group scales with MXFP4 weights (
[Bug][Humming] MXFP4 weight + block-FP8 activation is listed as supported on Hopper, but humming-kernels 0.1.16 rejects it
#60600
). Group-wise scales are also 1.2x to 24x slower than per-token in the SM90 Humming GEMM at M >= 256 (numbers in the review reply).
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG
still works as on main, with no early check: a format Humming cannot run fails while the weights convert, as before. With
--moe-backend humming
, setting it together with
moe.activation
is an error.
gpt-oss is unchanged. With no name, nothing changes.

I think it is interesting to support this, but I am a bit skeptical about how safe it is to make it the default, i.e., assume per-token FP8 quantization has no accuracy impact over BF16/grouped-FP8.
Notably, on Blackwell where FP8 activations are already the default, we use MXFP8 (group-32 e8m0 scales), or block-FP8 (group-128); both much finer-grained than one scale per token row. I suspect per-token FP8 is too coarse, and GSM8K is simply not a rigorous enough eval to study real accuracy impact.
I would either make the per-token FP8 path opt-in for now, or evaluate this more exhaustively before making it default, e.g. on agentic evals.

🐛 Describe the bug
HummingExpertsBase._supports_quant_scheme()
lists MXFP4 weights with block-FP8 activations (group 128, float32 scales) as a supported MoE pair. The comment says it works on Hopper (
fused_humming_moe.py#L325-L328

# (group-128 float32). Runs via WGMMA software dequant, so it

,
kFp8Dynamic128Sym
),
tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py
(from
#51332
) asserts that this pair is allowed.
humming-kernels 0.1.16 refuses the pair.
is_humming_schema_compatible()
in
humming/schema/humming.py
(lines 499 and 501) requires group-wise input scales to be e8m0 or e4m3 when the weights are FP4 with group scales:

bs_dtype
:

kFp8Dynamic128Sym
with MXFP4 weights, and the run then fails at weight load in
check_and_fallback_input_schema()

When the compatibility check is bypassed, a dense MXFP4 GEMM with group-128 float32 input scales runs on H200 and its output matches the reference (kernel error 0.0017-0.0032, the same level as per-token FP8). So the mismatch is between vLLM's supported-pairs table and humming's schema rule, not a missing kernel.
A related limit on SM90: MXFP8 inputs (group 32, e8m0 scales) pass

but have no SM90 kernel.
humming/tune/candidate.py:287

Is e8m0 input-scale support on WGMMA planned? Without it, MXFP8 activations cannot run on Hopper.

#59488

select the Humming MoE activation format for MXFP4 checkpoints. Until this is settled, it refuses

and
mxfp8
on SM90 Humming at startup.

Purpose
Package the SM90 mHC prenorm GEMM register-lifetime fix from
deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#448
, authored by jason (leevan). In a multi-stage K loop, the next iteration can overwrite register A operands before the previous asynchronous WGMMA has finished. Repeated calls with identical inputs can therefore produce different outputs. The upstream fix waits immediately after committing the WGMMA batch.
This integrates that existing fix into vLLM's packaged JIT header until the pinned DeepGEMM dependency contains it; it is not a new kernel implementation. DeepGEMM
#448
is currently open. Remove the temporary integration once the dependency pin includes the fix.
This correctness change was split out of
vLLM #58986
, which now contains only the H20 block-FP8 MoE tuning. This branch starts from main
07f1ba2ec66776650a490630ddfa9e3c92713c33
and does not depend on that performance PR. The corresponding v0.30 backport remains
mengziheng/vllm#3
. There is no throughput improvement claim for this correctness repair.
Changes
Generate a patched header during CMake configuration and install it without modifying a supplied
DEEPGEMM_SRC_DIR
. Exclude the original header from the directory install to prevent a same-timestamp overwrite.
Use the same helper in the standalone DeepGEMM installer. Recognized patched input is idempotent; unrecognized source fails without overwriting the destination.
Extend the existing mHC suite with six SM90 regressions: 256/512/1024 tokens, different split-K counts, default and side streams, independent FP32 references and exact repeatability. Skip when DeepGEMM is unavailable.

tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py

tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py

6 passed, 212 deselected

The broader selection returned

A fresh-process audit of the complete mHC operation covers 12 shape/seed groups with five repeats each. Repaired results are exactly repeatable; the original produces inconsistent results at 256/512 tokens. This does not establish whole-model token determinism.
An installation fixture using the actual CMake integration verified installed bytes equal the upstream fix, repeated configure/install preserves it, and supplied source content remains unchanged. The corrected control completed

. Those performance differences belong to the MoE tuning, with this fix present in both arms.
B200, production traffic, long soak tests and full-model serving on latest main were not validated.

vLLM has no MegaMoE that runs on Hopper today:

Details
Kernel.
FlashInfer
Sm90PullFp8MegaMoeConfig
, with FP32 128x128 weight scales and a SwiGLU clamp.
FlashInfer's push-style SM90 backend has no SwiGLU clamp, so it cannot serve
swiglu_limit
models.
Weights.
The kernel wants FC1 rows interleaved as
[pair, {gate, up}, 8]
under one 128x128 scale. Each scale block therefore covers rows from two checkpoint blocks, and both use
max(s_gate, s_up)
.
This is exact for power-of-two scales, which GLM-5.3-Flash has. Other checkpoints get one extra E4M3 rounding on half of the FC1 rows.
Workspaces.
The kernel always processes its whole token buffer, with a launch geometry picked for that size. With a single buffer sized at
max_num_batched_tokens
, decode is slower than the baseline.
The adapter therefore adds 64-, 256- and 1024-token workspaces. Each call uses the smallest one that fits the largest batch across DP ranks. Without DP-wide token counts it uses the default workspace, because every rank must pick the same buffer.
Loaders.
The fp8, compressed-tensors, online FP8 and Quark FP8 MoE methods now call the experts'
process_weights_after_loading
. It is a no-op for other experts.
The SM90 path is chosen from the quant config, not the weight dtype. FP8 weights keep their dtype, so a rebuild from preprocessed weights picks the same path.
Idle ranks.
With pass-through stages, the experts own the EP collective. A rank without tokens therefore still enters them. The change is identical to the one in
[Beam] Enable CuTeDSL NVFP4 MegaMoE
#62073
.
Limitations.
The backend needs expert parallelism and
nvshmem4py
.
It rejects DBO, runtime weight transfer and
apply_router_weight_on_input
.
Shared experts are not fused.
FlashInfer's SM90 input staging is torch-composed, about 1.2 ms per step at C128.

Follow-up to

(SM90 FP4 MegaMoE):
Cleanup fix:
with
single_active_dispatch_warp
, the inactive dispatch warp cleaned the workspace with empty expert counts and left pool blocks ≥ 32 of hot experts stale, so the next launch failed (H20, 97–128 tokens per rank, e.g. CUDA-graph capture); it now fetches the counts first (outputs bitwise unchanged, timing within noise).
H200 push dispatch:
add measured H200 EP8 buckets that enable push for M ≤ 32 on DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiMo-V2.5-Pro, and M ≤ 64 on DeepSeek-V4-Pro (rotated pool at M 33–64), saving about 10 µs per call (1.03–1.16x kernel time, bitwise-identical outputs; H20 and EP4 plans unchanged).
Other models:
accept any expert count that divides across ranks, keep the selected plans compilable for untuned geometries (H20 buckets match the full geometry, the
BLOCK_M=8

Summary
Batch-invariant mHC mixing statistics for DeepSeek-V4.1's hyper-connection layers, in
mhc.py
:
hc_mix_stats
computes the per-row mixing projections and sum of squares over a fixed number of K slices with
tf32x3
dots, so a row's result is bitwise identical whether computed alone or in a batch;
hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn
fuses the slice reduction with the sinkhorn normalisation that
hc_split_sinkhorn
performs.
Two compensated variants of the same projection for large batches, keeping the fp32 weight exact on the tensor cores:
hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_bf16x3
(Triton, three bf16 weight components, one activation read) and
hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn_deepgemm
(tf32 high part plus fp32 residual through DeepGEMM), with
split_bf16_hc_weight
/
split_tf32_hc_weight
preparing the weight parts. Both accumulate over
_HC_MIX_COMPENSATED_SLICES
and share the sinkhorn reduce kernel; sizes come from the input shapes and
hc_mult
.
hc_split_sinkhorn
answers an empty batch directly instead of launching a zero-sized grid, which the TileLang backend rejects.
Changes to existing kernels
hc_split_sinkhorn
: the empty-batch return only. Its existing caller already returns before reaching it with no tokens, so results on existing models are unchanged; the guard is for callers that do not pre-check.
Verification
Sinkhorn arithmetic (eps placement, iteration count, RMS scaling order) matches the existing Triton
hc_split_sinkhorn
port and the reference implementation.
The two compensated variants produce bitwise identical outputs to their previous standalone-module versions for M in {4096, 5000, 8192} (bf16x3) and {128, 1000, 4096} (DeepGEMM) at K = 20480.
test_mhc_kernels.py
and
test_hc_combine.py
cover the untouched kernels of the module.

Motivation
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Hopper spends substantial decode time in group32 dense GEMMs, capacity-sized indexer work, mHC statistics, and padded Marlin MoE projections. This PR tunes those paths. On Blackwell, flattened prefill selection also launches separate mask, sort, slot-map and raw-offset operations; the added integer kernel combines them.
Changes
Tune Hopper group32 GEMMs and reuse exact BF16 expansions of eligible FP8 weights, preserving activation quantization boundaries and the original fallbacks.
Use live paged indexer lengths and variable-length top-k; fuse masking, sorting and slot mapping.
Enable guarded Hopper mHC combine/norm and compensated BF16 projection paths, with decode statistics overlap.
Preserve intermediate activation rounding in fused clipped SwiGLU; defer MXFP4 padding until Marlin repacking.
On SM100-family CUDA GPUs, fuse flattened prefill selection into one integer kernel. Keep the changing visible slot count as a non-specialized runtime argument, so new context lengths do not create new JIT variants. Hopper retains its existing Torch selection path.

The Hopper derived caches trade GPU memory for throughput. # every (tile_n, n_thr) pair is one more kernel to compile. Tuned on GB300
# (hc_mult 4, hidden_size 5120 and 7168) against the separate post + split-k
# GEMM it replaces; the bands are coarse because the loss against a per-shape
# optimum is ~1-2%, while one fixed config gives up to 18% at the top of the
# range.
_FUSED_POST_PRE_N_THR = 128
_FUSED_POST_PRE_MAX_TOKENS = 32


def mhc_fused_post_pre_split_config(
    num_tokens: int, hidden_size: int, hc_mult: int
) -> tuple[int, int, int] | None:
    """Pick ``(tile_n, n_splits, n_thr)`` for the fused post + pre-norm GEMM.

    Returns None when a separate post kernel followed by a split-k GEMM is the
    better choice, or when the hidden size does not divide evenly across the
    fused kernel's block. One source of truth for the dispatch decision, the
    compile key and the launch, which must agree.
    """
    if num_tokens > _FUSED_POST_PRE_MAX_TOKENS:
        return None
    n_thr = _FUSED_POST_PRE_N_THR
    if hidden_size % n_thr:
        return None
    # The projection tiles supply the parallelism a small token count cannot,
    # so the tile grows with the batch: 1.3x at one token and 1.03x at 32
    # against a split-k GEMM given the split its own estimator computes.
    if num_tokens < 16:
        tile_n, n_splits = 2, 8
    else:
        tile_n, n_splits = 6, 8
    # The kernel drops projection tiles and k-slices it cannot fill evenly.
    mix_size = hc_mult * (hc_mult + 2)
    while tile_n > 1 and mix_size % tile_n:
        tile_n -= 1
    while n_splits > 1 and hidden_size % (n_splits * n_thr):
        n_splits //= 2
    return tile_n, n_splits, n_thr
